exercise.name: Bodyweight Standing Hip Extension
aliases: Standing leg extension to the back

reference.title: Bodyweight Standing Hip Extension (VERSION 2)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg goes back, inhale as it returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s back, 0.6 s hold, 1.4 s return

prescription.progression: Ankle weight, then a resistance band or cable kickback

cues.text: Stand tall on the left leg facing a wall, hands resting lightly on it, brace.
Breathe out and move the straight right leg back from the hip.
Squeeze the glute. Stop before the low back arches; the trunk stays tall.
Breathe in and bring the leg back under the hip with control.
Tap the toes down, reset, repeat; then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to swing the leg higher
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the ribs down; the leg only goes back about 15-20 degrees from the hip.
Stay tall; only a small forward tip of the pelvis is normal.
Slow, controlled lift and a pause at the back.
Keep the toes pointing down and forward so the hip does not rotate.

kinematics.norm: True hip extension is small, about 10-20 degrees with the knee straight, before the pelvis has to tip (clinical opinion)
Thigh angle behind vertical includes the small forward tip of the pelvis (clinical opinion)
Tall trunk; the pelvis may tip forward a few degrees, no lumbar arch (clinical opinion)
Moving knee straight; stance knee soft (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled with a short hold (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #646212, Bodyweight Standing Hip Extension (VERSION 2), video (movement reference)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Good balance: hands on hips instead of the wall.
Low back discomfort: make the movement smaller and brace first.
regressions: Prone hip extension on the floor.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Moving-leg hip extensor. Glute cues and abdominal bracing raised gluteus maximus activity in body-weight hip extension exercises (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the knee straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Stance-leg abductor holding the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the low back from arching as the leg goes back; a lumbopelvic control strategy raised gluteus maximus activity in related exercises (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk tall; they should not take over by arching the low back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk tall; they should not take over by arching the low back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Balance on the stance foot (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Leg sweeps back from the hip
